messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: P1 alert: KV cache runaway detected impacting continuous batching for multiple models. Symptoms: rising OOM/evictions, batch size oscillation, 95/99 latency spikes, and increased 502s for some customers. Affected variants: mistral-v3-gqa, qwen-mqa. Paging oncall @Alex (primary) and @Jia (backup).

Alex: on it. seeing a bunch of LRU evictions and contbatch queue length growth in the graphs. where did the fast prefetch/batch-change deploy land today?

Jia: rolled a batch-config tweak at 08:12 (commit 8f3b2a4) aimed to increase prefetch buffer for MQA workloads. thought it would help throughput, not this.

Priya: quick summary from cust telemetry: 3 enterprise customers in us-west saw 5-10x tail latency increases starting ~08:18 and some reported partial timeouts. no 100% outage but degraded. recommend throttling prefetch and forcing KV cache grace TTL to avoid spiral.

Mateo: digging in metrics. Redis keyspace shows rapid key churn; prefix-cardinality up 14x. KV hit rate dropped from 96% to 41% in 6 minutes. Continuous-batch dispatcher shows batch sizes growing then collapsing; backlog is triggering larger prefix warmups which then evict older prefixes -> positive feedback loop.

Alex: that sounds like a classic cache-regeneration spiral. options: rollback the 08:12 deploy, patch dispatcher to cap prefetch per-client, or temp fallback to smaller model-variant routing. which is fastest?

Jia: rollback should be fastest. I can revert the batch-config change and deploy a hotfix. rollback tag: revert/batch-config-08-12.

Priya: while rollback goes, let's mitigate customer impact by: 1) set contbatch.max_prefetch=2 for MQA routes 2) enable strict kv-grace-ttl=30s 3) set model routing preference to mistral-fallback for Qwen-heavy routes. Mateo, can you run those config flags as feature-flips?

Mateo: applying flips now. commands:
```bash
# set per-route prefetch
redwood-flip set route:mqa.contbatch.max_prefetch 2 --env prod
# tighten kv grace ttl
redwood-flip set kv.grace_ttl_seconds 30 --env prod
# route fallback for qwen-heavy customers
redwood-flip set routing.qwen_fallback mistral-v3 --env prod
```

DeployBot: Deploy started for revert/batch-config-08-12 by @Jia. CI passed. Rolling to prod canary.

Alex: monitoring. watch tail latency and kv.hit_rate on those prefixes. Also please watch for any increase in coldstart requests.

Mateo: quick metrics after flips (08:27): kv.hit_rate up from 41% -> 68% within 90s, contbatch backlog down ~60%, 95p latency trending down but still ~2x baseline. eviction rate reduced.

Jia: rollback completed at 08:30. hotpatch applied to cap prefetch and grace TTL.

Priya: starting customer notifications draft: short note explaining degraded latencies affecting some inference requests, mitigation in progress, next update in 30m. @Sam can you review?

Sam: reviewed. send it with link to status page and temporary mitigation notes, avoid deep technical details. 

Alex: good job. keep monitoring for 30 minutes. Mateo, please capture a timeline + artifacts for postmortem: graphs, prefix cardinality, 08:12 deploy diff, flip changes, and canary logs.

Mateo: saving artifacts and pushing to /incidents/2991234567/artifacts.tar.gz. snippets:
```json
{"prefix_cardinality": 14230, "eviction_rate_per_min": 980, "kv_hit_rate": 0.68}
```

IncidentBot: P1 status changed -> mitigated (active fixes in prod). No automated page escalation.

Priya: handing off to night oncall @Jia at 03:00Z for follow-up and postmortem work. recommended sev->postmortem: yes, root cause candidate: aggressive prefetch buff + contbatch interaction with high-prefix-cardinality MQA workloads (model-specific cold-warm churn for qwen-mqa).

Jia: ack handoff. I'll own postmortem and follow-ups. plan: reproduce in staging with synthetic Qwen-MQA traffic, add safety caps in dispatcher, and add automatic kv-throttle if prefix churn > X.

Alex: thanks all. final note: consider adding model-specific prefetch profiles rather than a global increase next time. :thumbsup: 

DeployBot: rollback/batch-config-08-12 completed at 08:30 by @Jia.

Sam: sending customer notifications now. will update thread with status page link.

Mateo: last check at 08:39: 99p latency back to near baseline for majority, 502s reduced to normal. leaving monitoring dashboard pinned for the night.

IncidentBot: thread closed for active work; open for postmortem comments.
